title: Beyond Locality: Feature-Boundary Auditing for OS-Integrated AI
abstract: arXiv:2606.10173v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: On-device inference reduces exposure to remote infrastructure, but it does not establish privacy for an operating-system assistant that aggregates cross-application data, retains derived state, or delegates actions. We present a feature-boundary audit method for OS-integrated AI. It combines a taxonomy of six privacy-failure surfaces, a five-dimension control rubric with separate evidence grades, and explicit records for adjacent data and authority paths. We apply the method to Apple Foundation Models, Apple Private Cloud Compute, Android AICore/Gemini Nano, and Microsoft Recall using primary public documentation. The analysis distinguishes request isolation from contextual restraint, retained-state controls from non-retention, and attestation from task-appropriate disclosure. A formative comparison of two 20-item assessment records identifies ambiguities in notice, retention, path ownership, and accountability. The source-link

translated_title: 超越本地化：面向操作系统集成AI的功能边界审计
translated_abstract: 设备端推理减少了对远程基础设施的暴露，但对于聚合跨应用数据、保留派生状态或委托执行操作的操作系统AI助手而言，这并不能真正确立隐私保护。我们提出了一种面向操作系统集成AI的功能边界审计方法。该方法结合了六个隐私失效面的分类体系、带有独立证据等级的五维控制评估准则，以及对相邻数据与权限路径的显式记录。我们基于一手公开文档，将该方法应用于Apple Foundation Models、Apple Private Cloud Compute、Android AICore/Gemini Nano以及Microsoft Recall。分析区分了请求隔离与上下文克制、保留状态控制与非保留策略，以及远程证明与任务适当的披露。对两份各含20项条目的评估记录进行形成性比较后，发现了在告知义务、数据保留、路径所有权与问责归属方面存在的模糊之处。
tldr: 该论文提出了一种面向操作系统集成AI的功能边界审计方法，通过隐私失效面分类体系、五维控制评估准则以及数据与权限路径记录，系统评估了苹果、谷歌、微软等主流操作系统级AI助手的隐私保护边界，并揭示了告知、保留、路径所有权与问责方面的模糊之处。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a feature-boundary audit method for OS-integrated AI—combining a taxonomy of six privacy-failure surfaces, a five-dimension control rubric with evidence grades, and explicit records of adjacent data and authority paths—and applies it to Apple Foundation Models, Apple Private Cloud Compute, Android AICore/Gemini Nano, and Microsoft Recall, revealing ambiguities in notice, retention, path ownership, and accountability.
